siteCopy.heroManifesto: WEAVENEX is a diversified and research-based architectural and design firm established in 2024. Founded by our Principal Architect, Architect Joshua De Guzman, and his peers, we are committed to functional planning and design excellence, innovation, and sustainability. We believe that each project is weaved through connection and understanding of its site, its client and its cultural and technological environment.We have a team of dedicated and talented architects and subordinates that thrives through the passion of the craft. Our company works on a wide range of project types from industrial, residential, hospitality, commercial, mixed-use developments, landscape architecture, and interior design.
siteCopy.architectsSubtitle: Every commission is led directly by our six founding architects—uniting monumental formwork, structural engineering, and raw material mastery without delegation.
siteCopy.commissionSubtitle: We accept a limited number of civic, cultural, and private brutalist commissions each year. Share your site parameters and program requirements directly with our six principals.

projects.title:
MIZU NO WA
水の輪 · Circle of Water
projects.summary: A contemporary pavilion inspired by the harmony between water, architecture, and the surrounding landscape. Its circular form represents continuity, while its open structure creates a seamless connection between people and nature.
projects.structuralNotes: Post-tensioned concrete trusses span 24 meters column-free over the main public atrium, weathered to deepen in tone over decades.

projects.title: Bendo Group of Companies Headquarters
projects.summary: Designed with a bold brutalist-inspired approach, the building showcases sculptural concrete volumes, dramatic cantilevered forms, and angular exterior circulation that create a distinctive and dynamic architectural identity.
projects.structuralNotes: Deep rock-anchored concrete piers transfer wind and thermal loads directly into the basalt bedrock below.

projects.title: Aurelia Concrete Sanctuary
projects.materials: Raw Architectural Concrete · Honed Dark Granite
projects.summary: A meditative brutalist sanctuary where soaring raw concrete colonnades and precision-cut roof apertures transform harsh tropical sunlight into sculptural shafts of shadow.
projects.structuralNotes: Zero applied finishes; every formwork tie-hole and aggregate seam is exposed as an honest structural record.

projects.title: Vanguard Brutalist Citadel
projects.summary: Twin cantilevered monoliths suspended above a sunken concrete plinth, housing next-generation design laboratories and fortified collaborative studios in the heart of BGC.
projects.structuralNotes: Steel plate girders embedded within 600mm concrete shear walls isolate laboratory floors from urban vibration.

projects.title: Sierra Mirror Monolith
projects.summary: Defined by a razor-sharp concrete volume cantilevered above a still black-granite reflecting pool, this highland residence balances raw monumental mass with quiet, mirror-like stillness.
projects.structuralNotes: Deep stepped concrete retaining walls anchor the cantilevered viewing deck into the mountain ridge while framing an uninterrupted water reflection.

projects.title: Bastion Residence
projects.materials: Pigmented Cast Concrete · Honed Black Basalt
projects.summary: A soaring concrete residential house anchored by a cantilevered oxidized corten-steel staircase and coffered skylight grid, leading into an atmospheric ribbed-concrete gallery spine.
projects.structuralNotes: Exposed concrete waffle skylights channel raking daylight across 18-meter shear walls while linear ceiling luminaires articulate the structural ribs after dusk.

architects.name: AR. JOSHUA S. DE GUZMAN
architects.bio: Leads the firm’s civic and institutional commissions. His work focuses on load-bearing honesty, massive cantilevered geometry, and structures built for a 200-year lifespan.

architects.name: AR. JAIRO C. ESPELIMBERGO
architects.bio: Specializes in brutalist private residences anchored into rugged coastal, alpine, and desert terrain, balancing raw thermal mass with razor-sharp steel glazing.

architects.name: AR. JOHN VINCENT R. BORBON
architects.bio: Choreographs natural daylight across monumental interior volumes. His pavilions and museums treat shadow and raw concrete mass as primary sculptural instruments.

architects.name: AR. LAWRENCE S. BERAQUIT
architects.education: M.Sc Structural Architecture, Politecnico di Milano
architects.bio: Bridges brutalist architectural expression with heavy structural engineering, pioneering post-tensioned concrete cantilevers and exposed steel exoskeletons.

architects.name: AR. RICH CHRISTIAN G. CARTUJANO
architects.bio: Directs the studio’s material research lab, developing custom timber formwork patterns, pigmented concrete mixes, and acoustic stone assemblies.

architects.name: AR. ADRIAN MIRAC G. AGAPAY
architects.bio: Shapes the threshold between brutalist architecture and the city, designing austere public plazas, subterranean transit concourses, and monolithic memorials.
